title: Fixes LP: #2116290 with a patch df-statfs-fallback.
description:
Fixes LP: #2116290 with a patch df-statfs-fallback.

Some chroots, specifically ones used in Launchpad, have absolute
paths in their /proc/self/mountinfo files. The default from_path()
method matches chroot-relative paths against absolute paths, which
always fails, causing LP: #2116290. This patch adds a statfs
fallback in this case to fix this bug. The original patch comes from
https://github.com/uutils/coreutils/pull/12072, but it has been slightly
modified to fix the Launchpad bug.
- d/patches: new patch that adds a statfs fallback

PPA: ppa:varranvar/patch2116290

The main testing is that df no longer throws errors on Launchpad
builds. Further testing is based on a best approximation of the bug.

test.sh ( a script for reproducing the bug):
```bash
set -e
 
UU_DF=/usr/lib/cargo/bin/coreutils/df
GNU_DF=/usr/bin/df
 
[ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ]  || { echo "Must be run as root." >&2; exit 1; }
[ -e "$UU_DF" ]        || { echo "Install rust-coreutils first." >&2; exit 1; }
 
CR=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$CR"' EXIT
 
# Copy a binary and its shared libraries into the chroot.
copy_bin() {
    local src=$1 dst=$2
    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dst")"
    cp "$src" "$dst"
    ldd "$src" 2>/dev/null | grep -o '/[^ ]*\.so[^ ]*' | while read -r lib; do
        [ -f "$lib" ] && cp --parents "$lib" "$CR/" 2>/dev/null || true
    done
}
 
copy_bin "$GNU_DF"                  "$CR/usr/bin/df"
copy_bin "$(readlink -f "$UU_DF")"  "$CR/usr/bin/coreutils"
cp --parents /lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2 "$CR/" 2>/dev/null || true
mkdir -p "$CR/usr/lib/cargo/bin/coreutils"
ln -sf ../../../../bin/coreutils "$CR/usr/lib/cargo/bin/coreutils/df"
 
# Directories mountinfo claims are mounted must exist for statfs() to work.
mkdir -p "$CR/dev/shm" "$CR/var/cache/apk" "$CR/etc/apk/keys"
mkdir -p "$CR/proc/self" "$CR/proc/1"
 
# Synthetic mountinfo: root ext4 FS only at sub-paths, no "/" entry.
DEV=$(python3 -c "import os; s=os.stat('/'); print(f'{os.major(s.st_dev)}:{os.minor(s.st_dev)}')")
cat > "$CR/proc/self/mountinfo" << EOF
22 1 0:50 / /dev rw - tmpfs tmpfs rw
23 22 0:51 / /dev/shm rw - tmpfs tmpfs rw
24 1 $DEV / /var/cache/apk rw,relatime - ext4 /dev/vda rw
25 1 $DEV / /etc/apk/keys rw,relatime - ext4 /dev/vda rw
EOF
ln -sf ../self/mountinfo "$CR/proc/1/mountinfo"
 
echo "--- uutils df / ---"
chroot "$CR" /usr/lib/cargo/bin/coreutils/df / 2>&1 && UU_EXIT=0 || UU_EXIT=$?
echo ""
echo "--- GNU df / ---"
chroot "$CR" /usr/bin/df / 2>&1 && GNU_EXIT=0 || GNU_EXIT=$?
 
echo ""
if [ "$UU_EXIT" -ne 0 ] && [ "$GNU_EXIT" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "BUG REPRODUCED (unpatched): uutils df / failed, GNU df / succeeded."
    exit 1
elif [ "$UU_EXIT" -eq 0 ] && [ "$GNU_EXIT" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "PASS (patched): both succeeded."
else
    echo "UNEXPECTED result: uutils=$UU_EXIT GNU=$GNU_EXIT" >&2
    exit 1
fi
```

GNU coreutils however behave a little +different here: it seems like they also use the statfs fallback +to find the filesystem that the path is on and then print the +last mountpoint in the mount table that is on the same filesystem. +Add such a fallback. + +In addition to the patch from the Github, add a final fallback to +from_path_direct() for the case where from_path_direct_with_mounts() +also fails. This happens in Launchpad build chroots where +/proc/self/mountinfo contains host-absolute mount paths that are +inaccessible from inside the chroot, causing statfs() calls on +mount_dir entries to fail. + +Bug-Ubuntu: https://launchpad.net/bugs/2116290 +Origin: other, https://github.com/uutils/coreutils/pull/12072 +Last-Update: 2026-06-03 +Forwarded: no + +--- a/src/uu/df/src/df.rs ++++ b/src/uu/df/src/df.rs +@@ -378,7 +378,9 @@ where + let fs_result = if use_fallback { + Filesystem::from_path_direct(path) + } else { +- Filesystem::from_path(&mounts, path) ++ Filesystem::from_path(&mounts, path) ++ .or_else(|_| Filesystem::from_path_direct_with_mounts(&mounts, path)) ++ .or_else(|_| Filesystem::from_path_direct(path)) + }; + #[cfg(not(unix))] + let fs_result = Filesystem::from_path(&mounts, path); +--- a/src/uu/df/src/filesystem.rs ++++ b/src/uu/df/src/filesystem.rs +@@ -227,6 +227,39 @@ impl Filesystem { + return result.and_then(|mount_info| Self::from_mount(mounts, mount_info, Some(file))); + } + ++ /// Fallback using statfs with a mount table available. ++ #[cfg(unix)] ++ pub(crate) fn from_path_direct_with_mounts

( ++ mounts: &[MountInfo], ++ path: P, ++ ) -> Result ++ where ++ P: AsRef, ++ { ++ let file = path.as_ref().as_os_str().to_owned(); ++ ++ let canonical_path = path ++ .as_ref() ++ .canonicalize() ++ .map_err(|_| FsError::InvalidPath)?; ++ ++ let stat_result = statfs(canonical_path.as_os_str()).map_err(|_| FsError::MountMissing)?; ++ ++ // GNU coreutils always appear to return the last match ++ let mut last_match = None; ++ for mount in mounts { ++ if let Ok(stat_result_mount) = statfs(&mount.mount_dir) ++ && stat_result_mount.fsid() == stat_result.fsid() ++ { ++ last_match = Some(mount); ++ } ++ } ++ ++ last_match ++ .ok_or(FsError::MountMissing) ++ .and_then(|mount_info| Self::from_mount(mounts, mount_info, Some(file))) ++ } ++ + /// Fallback using statfs when mount table is unavailable. + #[cfg(unix)] + pub(crate) fn from_path_direct
